classification.difficultyReason: The supplied diagram and explicit right-angle, distance and bearing stages guide the method; students still interpret reverse bearings and choose the final bearing direction.

content.prompt: Two boats at sea are both observing the same lighthouse, which is at a height of 220 m above sea level. From boat $A$ the bearing of the lighthouse is $040^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and the angle of elevation is $12^\circ$. From boat $B$ the bearing of the lighthouse is $310^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and the angle of elevation is $17^\circ$.

spec.description: Perspective scaffold with solid AO, OB and OC; dashed AC, CB and AB. North arrows and bearing cues occur at both boats, including a reflex cue at B. The given 12-degree elevation remains visible; other angle labels are to be completed.
spec.mathematics: OC is a vertical 220 m height. O is the lighthouse's sea-level projection. Bearings describe the horizontal directions AO and BO.
spec.answerVisibility: 040 degrees, 310 degrees and 17 degrees are withheld for completion.

answer.short: Label the bearing at $A$ as $040^\circ$, the clockwise reflex bearing at $B$ as $310^\circ$, and $\angle OBC=17^\circ$.
answer.worked: The bearings are measured clockwise from north to the horizontal sightlines $AO$ and $BO$. The $17^\circ$ elevation is between $BO$ and $BC$.

spec.description: Completion labels on the unchanged scaffold coordinate frame and bounding box.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Show that $\angle AOB=90^\circ$.

(Hint: draw the top-down bearing diagram of $\triangle AOB$.)

answer.worked:
At $O$, the reverse bearings give $OA$ a bearing of $220^\circ$ and $OB$ a bearing of $130^\circ$.

$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOB&=220^\circ-130^\circ\\&=90^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Horizontal triangle derived from the reverse bearings at O.
spec.mathematics: OA bearing 220 degrees and OB bearing 130 degrees differ by 90 degrees.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the distances $OA$ and $OB$ and hence $AB$, to the nearest metre.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Calculate $\angle OAB$ and hence the bearing of boat $B$ from $A$, to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\angle OAB&=\frac{OB}{OA}\\\angle OAB&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{220/\tan17^\circ}{220/\tan12^\circ}\right)\\&\approx35^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

$AB$ lies clockwise from $AO$, so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $40^\circ+\angle OAB\approx075^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
